items.summary: How strong must the shadow be? (our own pre-registered test, brain only, 8 Oct 2026): We lowered the input to the looming neurons step by step, from 80 to 10 spikes per second each. The turn command appeared from about 30 per second (38% of our strongest input) on both sides; below that the model did not turn. The escape neuron started firing at the same input as the turn command. A second seed agreed. Caveat in the chart: one model, brain only; the input is a rate we set for every LC4/LPLC2 of one eye, not a measured response to a real shadow; not a real fly; no measured real-fly rate found to compare. New chart and share card.

Relays silenced (brain only, 8 Oct 2026): With one relay neuron (PVLP141) silenced, the turn command stayed. With all 21-23 relay neurons between the looming neurons and the turn neuron silenced, the turn command stayed. Disclosed beside them: 'stayed' means the pre-registered turn rule still passed; the ratio we used saturates because the near-side turn neuron is always at 0 Hz; with PVLP141 silenced the far-side rate did fall (left 25 to 17 Hz, right 41 to 24 Hz).

The looming body test, now n 6: real map 6 of 6 turned away (left 3 of 3, right 3 of 3), scrambled 0 of 3 body runs (+3 drives identical to the floor); with the escape neuron silenced, the fly still turned away (2 of 2); with only the inside of the map scrambled, the fly turned away in 0 of 6 runs. The 5 Oct floor run repeated exactly. Updated walking chart.

Where in the wiring is the turn? (our own pre-registered test, brain only, 6 Oct 2026): We turned the scrambled maps up until they were as busy as the real one. They still did not produce the turn: the wiring, not the amount of activity, makes it. Also: Scrambling only the inside of the map kept about -9% of the turn command and 69% of the escape signal. (-9% means none: the far-side command was absent in all 6 trials) and With the escape neuron silenced, the turn command stayed. (expected: no giant fibre to DNa02 connections). Shown with every caveat in the chart: brain only, 7 drives await body runs, n per arm, a faster input checked first. New chart, census diagram and share card.

Our own pre-registered body test, Who does the walking?: the FlyGym fly walked 13.9 ± 0.58 mm in 1 s with the real brain (P9 stimulated), 14.15 mm with 3 scrambled brains that sent identical drives, 14.28 mm with a brainless constant drive and 13.96 mm with brainless random drives; the real brain added turning commands (DNa02); sugar sent no walking command (MN9 82 Hz) and the fly stood. The rate-to-drive mapping is ours and caps the drive. One stimulus, one model, one body, 1 s, open loop.

Sometimes: real fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 23 studies, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir and ML tasks it tied or lost (7).
